title: “JESUS LOVED HIM… AND LET HIM WALK AWAY.”
paragraphs: “JESUS LOVED HIM… AND LET HIM WALK AWAY.”

That line hits different when you realize—
He wasn’t a villain.
He wasn’t a rebel.
He wasn’t sleeping around or stealing from widows.

He was moral.
Disciplined.
Successful.
And still… he walked away from eternal life.
Let’s step into Gospel of Mark 10.

A wealthy young ruler runs to Jesus.
Runs.
Falls on his knees in the dust.
“Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
You can almost see him—robe flowing, sandals splashing through gravel, chest rising, eyes intense. Not arrogance. Hunger.
But he already thinks salvation is earned.
“What must I do?”

Jesus meets him where he stands. Lists the commandments.
And the young man responds with confidence:
“All these I have kept since I was a boy.”
Imagine the silence.
Then comes the line that shakes me every time:
“Jesus, looking at him, loved him…” (Mark 10:21)

Before correction—
Love.

Before confrontation—
Love.

Before exposing the idol—
Love.
That’s our Savior.

Not irritated.
Not rolling His eyes.
He loved him.
And because He loved him… He went for the root.
“One thing you lack. Go, sell everything you have, give to the poor… then come, follow Me.”
There it is.

Not a fundraising campaign.
Not anti-wealth rhetoric.
Heart surgery.

The issue was not money.
The issue was lordship.

The man wanted eternal life—
But he also wanted control.

He wanted Jesus as Savior…
Without Jesus as Treasure.
And Scripture says:
“He went away sorrowful, for he had great wealth.”

He didn’t argue.
He didn’t mock.
He just… walked away.
And Jesus let him.
Pause there.

Jesus didn’t chase him.
Didn’t negotiate.
Didn’t lower the standard.
Love does not beg idols to stay.

Some scholars interpret this moment as a demonstration that the Law cannot save—only Christ can. Others emphasize that wealth had become this man’s functional god. Both point to the same truth: you cannot cling to Jesus and your idol at the same time.
Family, hear me.
The most terrifying place to be is not open rebellion.
It’s respectful rejection.

You can kneel in front of Jesus…
And still walk away unchanged.

You can look clean on the outside…
And be chained on the inside.
This story isn’t about a rich man.
It’s about us.
What is the one thing you lack?
What is the one thing you refuse to release?

Relationship?
Reputation?
Career?
Secret addiction?
Control?
Jesus always exposes the one thing standing between you and surrender.
And He does it from love.
Let me say this gently but firmly:
If following Christ costs you nothing, you are not following the Christ of Gospel of Mark 10.
But here’s the Gospel turn.
When the disciples panic—“Who then can be saved?”—Jesus answers:
“With man it is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.” (Mark 10:27)
Translation?
You cannot save yourself.

Not by morality.
Not by generosity.
Not by effort.
The rich young ruler walked away sorrowful because he tried to earn what can only be received.
Eternal life is not purchased by selling possessions.
It is received by surrendering to a Person.

Jesus would soon give up everything—
Not because He lacked.
But because we did.

On the cross, the true Rich One became poor…
So spiritually bankrupt sinners like us could inherit the kingdom.
He did what the young ruler could not.

Perfect obedience.
Total surrender.
Absolute trust in the Father.
And now He says:
“Follow Me.”

Not “fix yourself.”
Not “impress Me.”
Not “buy your way in.”
Follow.
But understand this—He will lovingly put His finger on whatever competes with Him.
And if you walk away… He will let you.
Not because He doesn’t care.
But because love never forces worship.
Brother. Sister.
Don’t be the man who ran to Jesus and left unchanged.
Drop the idol.
Open your hands.
Repent. Believe. Follow.
He is worth more than everything you’re clinging to.

And unlike wealth—
He will never walk away from a heart that truly surrenders.
